Edge Functions are TypeScript (or JavaScript) functions running on Supabase's Deno-compatible edge runtime.
Where should a Supabase app call a third-party API that requires a secret key?
In an Edge Function that reads the key from secrets
In client code with the key in a VITE_ variable
Inside an RLS policy on the target table
In the metadata of a Storage bucket
Variables prefixed VITE_ are bundled into the browser code and become public. Edge Functions keep secrets on the server.
What does making a Supabase Storage bucket public do?
Lets anyone download files by URL without auth
Lets anyone upload, overwrite and delete its files
Lists all of its files on a public index page
Makes browsers cache its files forever
Public buckets skip access checks for downloads only. Uploads, updates and deletes are still governed by policies.
How is access to files in a private Supabase Storage bucket controlled?
With RLS policies on the storage.objects table
With a .htaccess file inside the bucket
With IAM roles assigned in the Google Cloud console
With a separate API key for each file
Storage keeps file metadata in Postgres, so the same RLS policy system controls who can read and write objects.
Which supabase-js Storage method creates a time-limited link to a file in a private bucket?
createSignedUrl
getPublicUrl
getSignedLink
createTempUrl
createSignedUrl(path, expiresIn) returns a URL valid for the given number of seconds. getPublicUrl only works for public buckets, and the other two methods do not exist.
After a user signs in with supabase-js, what does the client attach to its API requests?
A JWT access token for the user
The user's hashed password
The service_role key of the project
A database connection string
The access token identifies the user, so PostgREST and RLS can use auth.uid() and the authenticated role.
Where does Supabase Auth store user accounts?
In the auth.users table of the project database
In a separate MongoDB cluster managed by Supabase
Only in the browser's localStorage on each device
Automatically in the public.profiles table
Users live in the auth schema. A common pattern is a public.profiles table filled by a trigger on auth.users.
Which supabase-js method sends a passwordless email login link or one-time code?
signInWithOtp
signUpWithEmail
signInWithPassword
resetPasswordForEmail
signInWithOtp sends a magic link or a code, depending on the email template. signInWithPassword needs a password, and signUpWithEmail is not a supabase-js method.
What does supabase-js do when the user's access token is about to expire?
Uses the refresh token to get a new session
Logs the user out immediately and clears storage
Asks the user for the password again
Switches to the anon key for good
With autoRefreshToken on (the default), the client exchanges the refresh token for a new access token in the background.
Which open-source tool generates Supabase's REST API from the database schema?
PostgREST
Hasura
Prisma
PostGraphile
PostgREST turns tables, views and functions into REST endpoints automatically. Supabase's GraphQL API comes from the pg_graphql extension.
What does supabase.from('posts').select('id, title, author:profiles(name)') do?
Fetches posts with each author's name via the foreign key
Creates a view named author in the database for later
Runs two separate requests and merges their results in the client
Fails, since joins in supabase-js require raw SQL
PostgREST detects the foreign key between posts and profiles and embeds the related row. author: is an alias for the embedded resource.
firebase: How does Cloud Firestore store data compared with the Firebase Realtime Database?
Firestore uses collections of documents; RTDB is one JSON tree
Firestore is one JSON tree; RTDB uses collections of documents
Both store data as SQL tables with typed rows and columns
Firestore stores only strings; RTDB stores values of any type
Firestore organizes data into documents grouped in collections. Realtime Database stores everything as a single large JSON tree.
An app needs queries that filter on several fields and sort the results. Which Firebase database fits better?
Cloud Firestore
Realtime Database
Firebase Hosting
Cloud Storage for Firebase
Firestore supports compound queries with indexes. Realtime Database queries can only filter or sort on one property at a time.
What is the maximum size of a single Cloud Firestore document?
1 MiB
16 MB
100 KB
10 MB
A Firestore document can be at most 1 MiB. Larger content belongs in Cloud Storage or in subcollections.
Which of these paths points to a Firestore document rather than a collection?
users/alice/orders/order1
users/alice/orders
users/alice/orders/o1/items
teams/blue/members
Paths alternate collection and document, so document paths have an even number of segments.
You delete a Firestore document that has subcollections. What happens to the subcollections?
They remain and must be deleted separately
They are deleted automatically with the parent
The delete fails with a FAILED_PRECONDITION error
They move up into the parent collection
Deleting a document does not delete its subcollections. Use a recursive delete from the CLI or Admin SDK.
What does the Firestore rule allow read, write: if request.auth != null; permit?
Any signed-in user can read and write
Only the document owner can read and write
Only admins with custom claims can access
Nobody, until the rules are deployed
It checks only that a user is authenticated, not who they are, so any signed-in user can access every matched document.
Which rule on match /users/{userId} lets only that user read their own profile document?
allow read: if request.auth.uid == userId;
allow read: if resource.uid == true;
allow read: if request.time < userId;
allow read: if userId != null;
request.auth.uid is the caller's UID, and userId is the wildcard from the path, so the two must be equal.
Firestore rules allow reading posts only where published == true. A client queries all posts with no filter. What happens?
The query fails with a permission error
Only published posts are returned silently
All posts return, since rules apply to writes
Unpublished posts come back with empty fields
Rules are not filters: Firestore rejects a query that could return disallowed documents. The query must include where published == true.
Which Firestore web SDK function subscribes to live updates of a document?
onSnapshot
getDoc
onValue
watchDocument
onSnapshot calls your callback with the current data and again on every change. onValue is the Realtime Database equivalent, and watchDocument does not exist.
What should a React component do with the function returned by Firestore's onSnapshot when it unmounts?
Call it to stop the listener
Store it in Firestore for later
Pass it to getDoc to refresh
Ignore it, listeners stop themselves
onSnapshot returns an unsubscribe function. Not calling it leaks listeners and keeps billing reads.
A Firestore listener fires right after a local write, before the server confirms it. Which property shows this?
metadata.hasPendingWrites
metadata.fromCache
snapshot.isPendingSync
metadata.hasLocalChanges
Latency compensation fires local events immediately with hasPendingWrites set to true. fromCache means the data came from the local cache, and the other two properties do not exist.
In the Cloud Firestore Android and Apple SDKs, offline persistence is:
Enabled by default
Not supported at all
Only on paid plans
Disabled by default
Mobile SDKs cache data offline by default. In the web SDK it must be enabled explicitly.
A user writes data to Firestore while offline with persistence enabled. What happens?
Writes apply locally and sync when back online
Writes throw an error immediately
Writes are dropped after 60 seconds
Writes are sent through an SMS fallback channel
The SDK queues writes in the local cache, shows them to listeners right away and sends them when the connection returns.
Which Firebase Auth web function notifies your app when the user signs in or out?
onAuthStateChanged
onSnapshot
onUserLoaded
onIdTokenExpired
onAuthStateChanged runs on startup once the auth state is known and on every sign-in or sign-out, which suits route guards.
How should you grant an admin role that Firebase security rules can check securely?
Set a custom claim with the Admin SDK on a server
Store role: admin in the client's localStorage
Edit the ID token inside the browser
Make the user an Owner in project IAM
Custom claims are inside the signed ID token and appear as request.auth.token.admin in rules. Clients cannot change them.
How long is a Firebase Auth ID token valid before the SDK refreshes it?
One hour
Five minutes
24 hours
It never expires
ID tokens are short-lived JWTs that expire after one hour. The SDK refreshes them with a long-lived refresh token.
In Cloud Functions for Firebase (2nd gen), which trigger runs when a new Firestore document is created?
onDocumentCreated
onValueCreated
onObjectFinalized
onCall
onDocumentCreated comes from firebase-functions/v2/firestore. onValueCreated is for Realtime Database and onObjectFinalized is for Cloud Storage.
Why might a Cloud Function triggered on Firestore document updates run in an endless loop?
It writes to the same document that triggers it
It uses too many environment variables at once
It is deployed in a different region than the database
It returns a value instead of returning a promise
Each write fires the trigger again. Guard with a condition, for example skip when the field already has the new value.
What does a callable function (onCall) give you compared with a plain HTTP function?
The caller's Auth context passed in automatically
Unlimited invocations that are never billed
Direct access to the client's localStorage
Execution inside the user's own browser
The client SDK sends the ID token (and App Check token) and the function receives request.auth already verified.
Which Firebase database bills mainly by the number of document reads, writes and deletes?
Cloud Firestore
Realtime Database
Cloud Storage for Firebase
Firebase Hosting
Firestore charges per operation plus storage. Realtime Database charges mainly for stored data and downloaded bandwidth.
